title: Book 4 — Melpomene, Chapter 165
paragraphs: Meanwhile his mother Pheretime, while her son Arcesilaus—having brought evil on himself—was living at Barca, held her son's royal power at Cyrene, exercising his other rights and also sitting in council. But when she heard that her son had been killed at Barca, she left and fled to Egypt. For she could count on services rendered by Arcesilaus to Cambyses, son of Cyrus—since it was this Arcesilaus who had given Cyrene over to Cambyses and imposed tribute upon himself. Pheretime, therefore, coming to Egypt, sat as a suppliant of Aryandes, begging him to help her, and giving as her reason that it was because of her son's leaning toward the Medes that he had been killed.
